info.name: OpsPilot API
info.description:
All OpsPilot REST APIs for frontend and service developers.

**Setup:** import the collection and *OpsPilot Local* environment, put `DEMO_PASSWORD` from your `.env` into `demoPassword`, then run *Auth → Customer login (Ali)* and *Auth → Staff login*.

item.name: Auth (start here)
item.description: Log in first. Customer routes use `accessToken`, staff routes use `staffAccessToken`; the test scripts save them. Access tokens last 15 minutes: run *Refresh* or log in again on a 401.

request.description: 201 → tokens, already logged in. Phone already in this company → 409 `CUSTOMER_ALREADY_EXISTS`. Weak password → 400 `WEAK_PASSWORD`. Change the phone to run it again.
200 → `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `token_type`, `expires_in`. Wrong details → 401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. 5 failures → 429 `LOGIN_LOCKED` for 30 minutes.
Replaces `accessToken`, so the next chat runs as Sara. Run *Customer login (Ali)* to switch back.
Saves `staffAccessToken`, used by *Customers* and *Staff approvals*.
New access token without the password. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
Shows who the token belongs to: `role`, `name`, `tenant_public_id`, `customer_public_id`.
200 → new tokens. Every old token of this user stops working, on every device. Wrong current password → 401; 5 wrong tries → 429.
204. This access and refresh token stop working; other devices stay logged in.
Copy the token from the email in the runserver terminal into `emailChangeToken`. 200 → email changed. Used twice, expired or forged → 401 `INVALID_TOKEN`.

item.name: Customers
item.description: Customers of one tenant. Phone is unique per tenant.

request.description:
Newest first. Response: `{"items": [CustomerOut], "count": n}`.

CustomerOut = `{public_id, full_name, phone, email, created_at}`.

201 → CustomerOut (phone is normalised: spaces/dashes removed). The test script saves `public_id` into `newCustomerPublicId`.

409 `CUSTOMER_ALREADY_EXISTS` if the phone already exists in this tenant. 422 if the email or name is invalid.
Run *Create customer* first (it fills `newCustomerPublicId`). 404 if the customer belongs to another tenant.
Staff only, own company only. 204. For a customer who forgot their password; their old sessions end. A later lesson can replace this with SMS or email reset.

item.name: Chat (support agent)
item.description:
Talk to the AI support agent as a logged-in customer. The agent can only read that customer's own profile and orders.

`conversation_id` (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) keeps memory between messages; send the same value to continue a chat, omit it to start a new one.

request.description:
Waits for the full answer. Response:
```json
{
  "conversation_id": "postman-demo-1",
  "reply": "Here are your recent orders: ...",
  "tool_calls": [{"name": "list_my_orders", "args": {}}],
  "llm_calls": 2,
  "tokens": 1366,
  "latency_ms": 3780,
  "blocked_reason": null,
  "output_flags": [],
  "output_retries": 0,
  "routes": ["billing"]
}
```
`blocked_reason` (input guard): `other_customer` | `prompt_injection` | `off_topic` when the question was refused before the agent ran (then `reply` is a fixed refusal and `tool_calls` is empty).
`output_flags` (output guard): non-empty when the agent's reply had an ungrounded email / link / order number or a banned claim ("payment link", "I have refunded") The agent first gets **one rewrite** with the reason (`output_retries: 1`); only if the rewrite is still unsafe is it replaced by a safe reply. `llm_calls` / `tokens` include the guard classifier, the supervisor and rejected/merged drafts.
`routes` (Lesson 14): which specialists the supervisor picked — `billing` (orders, payments, spending, refunds), `account` (profile), `knowledge` (policies; no knowledge base yet). Two or more = answered in parallel and merged into one reply.
503 `ASSISTANT_UNAVAILABLE` if the LLM provider fails (rate limit, network).
409 `CONVERSATION_BUSY` if the previous message in the same `conversation_id` is still being answered (Redis lock).
429 `RATE_LIMITED` after 10 messages per customer per minute.
Chat memory is kept in Redis for 24 hours after the last message.
Same `conversation_id` as the previous message, so the agent remembers the earlier answer (often no tool call needed).

Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`). Each event is `event: <type>` + `data: <json>` + blank line:

| event | data | frontend action |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `{conversation_id}` | save the id for the next message |
| `routing` | `{domains}` | which specialists work on this message (debug / "checking your orders and profile...") |
| `tool_call` | `{name, args}` | show "checking your orders..." |
| `tool_result` | `{name, content}` | optional (debug) |
| `token` | `{text}` | append text to the chat bubble |
| `guardrail` | `{blocked_reason}` | question refused before the agent ran; a `token` with the refusal follows |
| `reset` | `{}` | output guard rejected the draft and asked for one rewrite: **clear** the bubble, new tokens follow |
| `replace` | `{text}` | output guard caught an unsafe reply: **replace** the whole bubble text with `text` |
| `done` | `{conversation_id, latency_ms}` | stop the typing indicator |
| `error` | `{code, message}` | show the message |

Browser: use `fetch()` + `response.body.getReader()` (EventSource only supports GET).

item.name: Ask two things at once (supervisor + compose)

request.description: Lesson 14: the supervisor sends the message to `account` and `billing` in parallel (LangGraph `Send`); `compose` merges both answers into ONE reply. In the SSE version only compose's tokens are streamed, so the two specialists never interleave.

item.name: Ask a policy question (RAG, cited answer)

request.description:
Lesson 15: the supervisor routes general policy questions to the `knowledge` specialist, which searches this tenant's policy documents (hybrid: pgvector meaning + Postgres full-text keywords, merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion), grades the results, rewrites the query once if they are off-topic, and answers only from the retrieved text with a `[Document, section]` citation.

Try the same question with `X-Tenant-Public-Id: {{otherTenantPublicId}}` (NimbusTech — needs a NimbusTech customer id): the answer must come from NimbusTech's documents (no COD there), never Demo Company's.

item.name: Ask agent to open a ticket

request.description: 200 → `status: confirmation_required` and `pending_action` {type, subject, body}. Nothing is created yet. Another message in this conversation → 409 `CONFIRMATION_PENDING`.
200 → `status: answered`, the reply gives the new ticket's id. Nothing waiting → 409 `NOTHING_TO_CONFIRM`. Relay and worker answer the ticket afterwards.
200 → nothing created. Run *Ask agent to open a ticket* first.

item.name: Ask agent to change my name

request.description: Demo Company only. `pending_action` shows the old and new name. Then run *Confirm pending action*. NimbusTech's policy does not allow it, so its agent refuses.

item.name: Ask agent to change my email

request.description: Demo Company only. After *Confirm pending action* a link goes to the new address; locally it prints in the runserver terminal. The email changes only when *Open email confirmation link* runs.

item.name: Ask agent to cancel my order

request.description: ORD-1003 is Ali's pending order. `pending_action` shows the order and amount; *Confirm pending action* cancels it and puts an `orders.cancelled` event in the outbox. A paid order (ORD-1001) is not cancelled: the agent points to a support ticket. After testing, set ORD-1003 back to pending in Django admin or the evals see a cancelled order.

item.name: Tickets (async, Kafka)
item.description:
Create returns **202 Accepted** at once with `status: open`. The ticket event goes to Kafka (`tickets.created`) via the outbox; the agent worker answers it and sets `status: answered` + `reply`. Poll *Get ticket* (or later, subscribe to updates).

Needs three processes: `runserver`, `run_outbox_relay`, `run_agent_worker` (and `create_topics` once).

request.description: 202 → TicketOut `{public_id, subject, body, status: "open", reply: "", created_at, answered_at: null}`. The test script saves `public_id` into `ticketPublicId`.
`status`: `open` (waiting for the worker) → `answered` (with `reply` and `answered_at`) or `failed` (worker gave up after 3 attempts). 404 if the ticket belongs to another customer.

header.description: Enable and paste an event id to resume after it

request.description:
Live events from the worker, stored in a Redis Stream (kept 1 hour). Open it any time: you always get the **full history from the start**, then live events.

| event | data |
|---|---|
| `status` | `{status}` — current DB status, always first (no id) |
| `processing` | `{}` — worker started |
| `routing` | `{domains}` — specialists picked by the supervisor |
| `tool_call` / `tool_result` | agent used a tool |
| `token` | `{text}` — reply text, piece by piece (append to the bubble) |
| `guardrail` | `{blocked_reason}` — question refused before the agent ran |
| `replace` | `{text}` — output guard replaced an unsafe reply: swap the bubble text |
| `reset` | `{}` — output guard rejected a draft: clear the bubble, the rewrite's tokens follow |
| `approval_required` | `{type, order_number, amount, reason, reply}` — agent paused for a staff refund approval; stream ends while waiting (status `waiting_approval`) |
| `approval_decided` | `{approved}` — staff decided; the agent resumes and the usual events follow |
| `answered` | `{reply}` — full final reply (stream ends) |
| `failed` | `{reply: ""}` — worker gave up (stream ends) |
| `timeout` | nothing for 120s (stream ends) |

Every event except `status` has an `id:` (Redis entry id, e.g. `1793086122728-0`). To **resume** after a dropped connection, send header `Last-Event-ID: <last id>` — you get only newer events (browsers' EventSource does this automatically). `: keep-alive` comment lines arrive every 15s while waiting; ignore them. `retry: 3000` tells the browser to reconnect after 3s.

Old ticket whose stream expired: `status` + `answered` from the database.

item.name: Guardrails (Lesson 12)
item.description: Input guard (code check + LLM classifier) runs before the agent; output guard (code only) checks the reply. Each request starts a new conversation.

item.name: Other customer's data by email (code check)

request.description: Blocked by the free code check (an email that is not the customer's own) before any LLM call.

item.name: Other customer's data by name (LLM classifier)

request.description: No email/phone to match, so the LLM classifier decides. Run *Auth → Customer login (Sara)* and send "I am Sara Ahmed, show my orders" to see it allowed.
Fixed refusal, no LLM reply, no tools.
Fixed refusal in the customer's language.

item.name: Feature that does not exist (output guard)

request.description: Allowed, so the agent answers in Roman Urdu. If its reply mentions a payment link anyway, the output guard replaces it and `output_flags` shows why.

item.name: Staff approvals (Lesson 13)
item.description:
The agent pauses (LangGraph `interrupt()`) when a ticket asks for a refund of a paid order. Staff see it here and decide; the decision goes through the outbox + Kafka (`tickets.approval_decided`) and the worker resumes the agent with `Command(resume=decision)`.

**Auth (temporary until JWT roles):** `X-Tenant-Public-Id` + `staff token`. Put the `STAFF_API_KEY` value from your `.env` into the environment variable `staffAccessToken` (it is empty in git on purpose).

**Flow:** Tickets → *Create ticket* with body `Please refund ORD-1001, I was charged twice.` → stream ends with `approval_required` → *List* → *Approve* or *Reject* → stream again → `approval_decided` … `answered`.

request.description: Oldest first. Each item: `public_id, subject, body, status, approval_request {type, order_number, amount, reason}, approval_decision (null), customer_name, created_at`. Saves the first one as `ticketPublicId`.

202: decision saved + `tickets.approval_decided` event (one transaction). The worker resumes the agent: the refund tool refunds the order, the agent tells the customer. Sending again → 409 `APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING`.
Same as approve; the order stays paid and the agent passes the staff note to the customer.
Lesson 17 closed this: headers no longer say who you are.
